title: CEO Pay Ratio Disclosures and Changes in Employee Pay Satisfaction
eligible_reason: Staggered binary treatment: treat = 1 in firm-months after the firm's first CEO pay ratio disclosure (proxy filing); the stacking code enumerates 12 monthly event cohorts (event_yearmonth 24218-24229, i.e. Feb 2018 to Jan 2019) in an 18-month firm-month panel of 1,360 firms. Table 4 column 2 is a static TWFE with firm and year-month fixed effects and no controls: reghdfe compensation_benefit_mean treat, absorb(gvkey yearmonth) cluster(gvkey yearmonth). All other reported columns add nine time-varying firm controls, interactions, or a stacked design, and are ineligible.
design_notes: Firm-month panel sample_employee_ym.dta restricted to active_sample==1 (N = 18,647 firm-months, 1,360 gvkey clusters, 18 yearmonth clusters per Stata log). Outcome: monthly mean Glassdoor compensation-and-benefits rating. Treatment 'treat' (Post Disclosure) = 1 once the firm has provided its initial pay ratio. Table 4: col 1 no FE, col 2 firm + year-month FE (ELIGIBLE), col 3 adds $control = size numsegs intangible bm firm_age analyst_coverage instown sue cash (time-varying, ineligible). Figure 1: event study treat_n4..treat_p3 with controls (ineligible). Table 5: Cengiz et al. (2019) stacked regression with group x firm and group x year-month FE and controls; fixed-window and backfilled samples with controls (all ineligible). Tables 6-8: treat interacted with pay-ratio, median-pay and information-environment variables plus controls (ineligible). Table 9: falsification samples with controls; private-firm comparison with a common April-2018 cutoff and firm FE only; work-life-balance and number-of-comments outcomes with controls (ineligible). Since the SEC mandate applied to all registrants, most or all sample firms are eventually treated; whether never-treated firms remain within the 18-month window is not determinable from the code.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: levelsof event_yearmonth in the Stata log: 24218 ... 24229 (12 consecutive months, Feb 2018 - Jan 2019).
never_treated_note: All public firms were required to disclose; whether some sample firms are untreated throughout the 18-month window cannot be checked without the data.
preferred_spec_note: Table 4 is the headline table; column 3 (with controls) is probably the authors' preferred column, column 2 is the eligible no-controls version.

published_estimates.source: Stata Log.log (real data run), Table 4 column 2

data_access_detail: README says the Data folder (sample_employee_ym.dta etc.) is included, but the downloaded archive (_archive_mnsc.2024.08151.zip, 5 files) contains only Read Me.docx, Stata Code.do, Stata Log.log, SAS Code.sas, SAS Log.log. Underlying sources: Glassdoor ratings (scraped), SEC proxy statements (public), Compustat/CRSP/IBES/13F/Execucomp/RavenPack (licensed). Rater salary data withheld under NDA (not needed for the eligible spec).
data_files_note: Expected per README but absent: Data/sample_employee_ym.dta (main), sample_employee_ym_fw.dta, sample_employee_ym_bfcb.dta, sample_employee_ym_fal.dta, sample_employee_ym_fal2.dta, rep_sample.dta, privateaverage_byfirms.dta. Check the INFORMS supplement for a separate data archive or contact the authors.
software_notes: Stata (reghdfe, outreg2, estout); SAS for dataset construction.
replication_feasible_note: Feasible if the firm-month file sample_employee_ym.dta can be obtained (README indicates the authors intended to ship it). Only one eligible spec; event-study version would need controls dropped.
priority_note: Eligible design (12 monthly cohorts) with one no-controls TWFE column, but the data file is missing from the downloaded package.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Cohort count from 'levelsof event_yearmonth' in Stata Log.log; sample sizes and coefficients from the log (real-data run). Modern-estimator flags in the frame (Baker-Larcker-Wang, Cengiz) correspond to the stacked robustness check, not CSA/BJS.
